nodes.description: Contract owner address, set to the deployer (msg.sender) in the constructor; also receives a 5 finney fee on a lost challenge.
Public mapping of player address to withdrawable balance in wei; credited on challenge wins/fees and zeroed on withdrawal.
Current leader/champion address; initialized to owner and replaced by the challenger when the pseudo-random flip is odd.
Constructor that assigns owner = msg.sender and leader = owner at deployment time.
View function returning balances[player] for an arbitrary address.
View function returning the current leader address.
Withdraw function: requires a positive caller balance, zeroes it (checks-effects-interactions) and then performs msg.sender.transfer(amount).
Payable challenge accepting exactly 100 finney; computes a pseudo-random value from blockhash, leader and msg.sender, then updates leader/balances accordingly.
Attacker-controllable caller address used as owner, withdrawer, challenge participant, balance key and transfer recipient.
msg.sender.transfer(amount) external value transfer; potential reentrancy/forced-interaction point inside userWithdraw.
Pseudo-randomness derived from blockhash(block.number - 1), leader and msg.sender; predictable/miner-influenceable block data driving fund distribution.
Unchecked balance increments (balances[msg.sender] += 100 finney, balances[leader] += 95 finney) with no SafeMath in Solidity 0.4.23.
Address parameter of publicGetBalance used to index the balances mapping.
Local variable in userWithdraw holding the caller balance that is transferred out.
Local variable in userChallenge holding the combined blockhash/leader/sender value whose parity decides the winner.

edges.reason: msg.sender is written into the owner state variable in the constructor.
userWithdraw uses msg.sender to look up the caller's balance and to gate the require check.
msg.sender is the recipient of the external transfer call, so the caller controls the value sink.
msg.sender is mixed into the pseudo-random value that determines challenge outcome and leader changes.
The external transfer is executed as the last statement of userWithdraw, handing control to the recipient.
The balances mapping is read and zeroed in the same function that performs the external call, coupling state and external interaction.
userChallenge builds its outcome from blockhash/block data, executing the weak-randomness operation.
The parity of the weak random value controls which branch (leader/balance update) executes.
The caller-controlled address keys the balance that is incremented by 100 finney on a win.
Unchecked increments mutate the balances mapping without overflow protection.
The balance increments are performed inside the winner branch of userChallenge.
userChallenge reassigns the leader state variable when the challenger wins.
userChallenge credits balances to the players and to owner depending on the random outcome.
The current leader address is incorporated into the random value used to decide the challenge.
The player parameter is used as the mapping key returned by publicGetBalance.
The local amount variable supplies the value sent in the external transfer.
The local random variable is computed from blockhash and drives the weak-randomness operation.

normalization_plan.reason: The player parameter has no standalone semantic role; it only indexes balances inside publicGetBalance, so it collapses into that function node.
The amount local variable is only an intermediate holder for the transferred value, so it is absorbed into the unsafe transfer operation.
The random local variable merely stores the blockhash-derived value, so it is absorbed into the weak-randomness unsafe operation.
